problem_statement: biazo/codrops-add-to-cart is a runnable Vite + GSAP single-page commerce demo: a six-item product grid animates each product into a fixed cart button, a cart drawer slides in with the chosen item, and plus/minus/remove controls drive an in-memory cart whose total updates from the cartItems state. The shop has been given a small-studio persona -- 'Ember & Oat', a maker of wood-fired ceramics, hand-loomed textiles and letterpress prints -- and a second Lookbook page that shares the same product grid. Build the store's own 'Shop by collection' browsing control: a filter bar that sits directly above the product grid with a row of collection tabs (All, Ceramics, Textiles, Prints) and a live count readout. Clicking a collection tab must show only the products in that collection (each product carries a data-collection of ceramics, textiles or prints, two per collection) and update the readout to read exactly 'Showing N of 6 · <Collection>' -- for example clicking Ceramics shows the two ceramics products and reads 'Showing 2 of 6 · Ceramics', while All reads 'Showing 6 of 6 · All collections'. The same filter bar must appear on both the Shop page and the Lookbook page. Preserve the GSAP add-to-cart fly animation, the cart badge, the sliding drawer, the quantity/remove/checkout controls and the in-memory cart logic exactly; the filter restyles the browsing surface, it does not replace the cart.
required_content: Add a 'Shop by collection' filter bar directly above the product grid (.products__list) on the Shop page, containing an eyebrow label 'Shop by collection', a live count readout, and a row of four collection tabs labelled All, Ceramics, Textiles and Prints, with the All tab active by default.

Tag each of the six products with its collection (two Ceramics, two Textiles, two Prints via a data-collection attribute) and filter the visible product cards to the chosen collection when its tab is clicked, keeping the existing product cards and cover images.

Drive a live count readout from the actual visible cards so it reads exactly 'Showing 6 of 6 · All collections' by default and, after clicking a collection tab, 'Showing N of 6 · <Collection>' (for example 'Showing 2 of 6 · Ceramics'); the active tab must move to the clicked collection.
Render the same 'Shop by collection' filter bar (with its tabs and readout) on the shared Lookbook page as well, so the browsing control is consistent across both shop surfaces.

Keep the filter bar and its tab row free of horizontal overflow at 390px mobile, wrapping the tabs onto multiple rows rather than forcing a fixed-width strip, and keep the active tab legible (readable contrast).

Preserve the GSAP add-to-cart fly animation, the cart button badge, the sliding cart drawer, the Quantity plus/minus controls, the Remove action, the Total readout and the Checkout button, all driven by the original cart logic.
Do not add a new cart library, persistence layer, framework router, modal system, dependency, remote asset, or generated image; reuse the existing local product images.
design_constraints: Work inside the existing source files and class conventions: src/index.html and src/lookbook.html host the grid, src/js/shopfilter.js wires the filter, and src/scss/shopfilter.scss styles it, alongside the existing cart files.
The filter must be the shop's own genre-native browsing control placed above the grid; it must not redesign the grid, replace the product cards, or add unrelated commerce surfaces.
The count readout must be recomputed from the products actually shown after each click, not from static text only.
Desktop (1440px), tablet (834px) and 390px mobile states must remain free of horizontal overflow and keep the tab controls reachable and legible.
state_constraints: desktop_initial verifies the Ember & Oat shop masthead, the 'Shop by collection' filter bar and the six product cards render before any interaction.
mobile_initial and mobile_shopfilter verify the filter bar and its tab row wrap cleanly at 390px with no horizontal overflow.
desktop_shopfilter verifies the default filter bar renders with the four collection tabs, the All tab active and the readout reading 'Showing 6 of 6 · All collections' above the full six-card grid.
desktop_shopfilter_ceramics clicks the Ceramics tab and verifies the grid filters to the two ceramics products while the readout updates to 'Showing 2 of 6 · Ceramics'.
desktop_lookbook verifies the same 'Shop by collection' filter bar with its four tabs appears on the shared Lookbook page.
desktop_cart_badge, desktop_cart_open, desktop_quantity_plus and desktop_remove_empty verify the GSAP add-to-cart animation, cart badge, drawer, quantity plus and remove still work.
tablet_cart_open and mobile_cart_open verify the open-cart drawer fits the responsive layout without clipping controls or creating horizontal overflow.

change_completion: The 'Shop by collection' filter bar renders above the grid with All/Ceramics/Textiles/Prints tabs and a live count readout, and appears on both the Shop and Lookbook pages.
Clicking a collection tab filters the visible product cards to that collection and updates the readout to 'Showing N of 6 · <Collection>', with the active state moving to the clicked tab.
experience_continuity: The count readout is recomputed from the products actually shown after each click ('Showing 2 of 6 · Ceramics' for Ceramics, 'Showing 6 of 6 · All collections' for All).
The GSAP add-to-cart animation, cart badge, drawer, quantity, remove and checkout continue to work alongside the filter.
design_consistency: The filter bar matches the monochrome editorial layout of the shop and sits naturally above the product grid on both pages.
The change does not redesign the whole page, replace product cards, or add unrelated commerce surfaces.
responsive: Desktop, tablet and 390px mobile states have no horizontal overflow.
The collection tab row wraps onto multiple rows on mobile while keeping every tab reachable and the active tab legible.
regression: npm install / vite build / static serve remains valid for the multi-page Vite app (index + lookbook).
Product images from static/images remain used, and the GSAP add-to-cart animation still updates the cart badge and cart item list.

author_notes: Slot slot_244 targets commerce / experience_continuity / restyle / section for the Edit capability on biazo/codrops-add-to-cart, a runnable Vite + GSAP add-to-cart shopping demo with a six-item product grid, cover images and a sliding cart drawer. The native lever is the shop's OWN 'Shop by collection' browsing control -- a collection filter bar (All / Ceramics / Textiles / Prints tabs plus a live 'Showing N of 6 · <Collection>' count readout) placed directly above the product grid, the genre-natural home for a category filter in a commerce storefront. The reference filters the product cards by data-collection and keeps the readout in sync, and ships the same filter bar on both the Shop page and a shared Lookbook page. The baseline keeps the filter wiring correct (its readout updates to 'Showing 2 of 6 · Ceramics' on click) but ships a broken filter-bar stylesheet (a fixed-width nowrap tab strip that overflows the mobile viewport and shingled, near-white-on-white tabs that overlap into an illegible pile) and drops the filter bar entirely from the Lookbook page. The known-bad control ships the same broken stylesheet AND a frozen filter: clicking a tab flips the active class (the click succeeds) but the readout is snapshotted once at construction and the grid is never filtered, so it stays 'Showing 6 of 6 · All collections' with all six cards visible, and it too drops the filter from the Lookbook page. The remote Typekit font <link> is retained as a console/network-clean stylesheet reference (allowlisted, identical across all three legs). The product images under static/images are reused; no cart library, dependency, route framework or generated image or asset is added.
